title: I spun up a free, read-only script to check WordPress sites for signs of PHP2Shell compromise. Looking for feedback
description: This content describes a free, read-only bash script designed to triage WordPress sites for signs of compromise related to the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) and a third CVE-2026-115560. The script checks PHP versions, WordPress core and plugin integrity, suspicious PHP files in uploads, recent file modifications, common web-shell patterns, user accounts, cron jobs, logs, Docker containers, and configuration settings relevant to the vulnerabilities. It generates detailed Markdown reports without modifying the target systems. The PHP2Shell vulnerabilities are critical remote code execution bugs patched in PHP releases 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12, but the third CVE has no fixed build yet, with a recommended mitigation of setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0. The script helps detect potential backdoors planted before patching, as updating PHP alone does not remove them.
